chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from 'Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Maysarah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If a woman is found in a barren place where there is no one, and I ask her, "Do you have a husband?" and she says, "No," then I marry her.' He said: 'Yes, she is the one verifying it upon herself.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ع: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), referring to Imam al-Sadiq
key_terms.الْمُصَدِّقَةُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهَا: The one who verifies/testifies regarding herself

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a woman found alone without witnesses to her marital status?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar establishes the principle of 'istishhab' (presumption of continuity) regarding a woman's marital status, where her self-declaration of being unmarried is accepted as valid evidence for marriage. It highlights the Shia juristic view that a woman has the authority to testify regarding her own personal status in the absence of external witnesses, reflecting the practical application of legal presumption in family law.
